facts.statement: The genus Torosaurus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1891.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1891

facts.statement: Fossils of Torosaurus have been found across the Western Interior of North America, ranging from Saskatchewan to Texas.
facts.quote: Fossils which have been definitively identified as Torosaurus or which might belong to it have been discovered across the Western Interior of North America, from as far north as Saskatchewan to as far south as Texas

facts.statement: Torosaurus measured between 7.5 and 9 meters in length and weighed approximately 8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Measuring between 7.5 and 9 m and weighing around 8 MT

facts.statement: In 1891, John Bell Hatcher discovered a pair of ceratopsian skulls with elongated, perforated frills in Niobrara County, southeastern Wyoming.
facts.quote: In 1891, two years after the naming of Triceratops, a pair of ceratopsian skulls with elongated frills bearing holes were found by John Bell Hatcher in Niobrara County in southeastern Wyoming

facts.statement: The name Torosaurus is likely derived from the Greek verb 'toreo,' meaning 'to perforate,' rather than being a mistranslation of 'bull lizard'.
facts.quote: The name Torosaurus is frequently mistranslated as "bull lizard" from the Latin noun taurus or the Spanish word toro, but is much more likely derived from the Greek verb (toreo), which means "to perforate"

facts.statement: The name alludes to the 'window-like' holes in the elongated frill, which traditionally distinguish Torosaurus from the solid frill of Triceratops.
facts.quote: The allusion is to the fenestrae, "window-like" holes, in the elongated frill, which have traditionally served to distinguish it from the solid frill of Triceratops

facts.statement: The type species T. latus is based on holotype YPM 1830, which is a partial skull.
facts.quote: T. latus was based on holotype YPM 1830, which is a partial skull

facts.statement: The holotype for T. gladius was specimen YPM 1831, which is an even larger skull than the type species.
facts.quote: The holotype of T. gladius was specimen YPM 1831, which is an even larger skull

facts.statement: The holotypes for both T. latus and T. gladius were found in the Lance Formation of the late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Both fossils were found in the Lance Formation of the late Maastrichtian

facts.statement: In 2010, a study suggested that Torosaurus might represent the mature growth stage of Triceratops, rather than a separate genus.
facts.quote: In 2010, the validity of Torosaurus was disputed. A study of fossil bone histology combined with an investigation of frill shape concluded that Torosaurus probably represented the mature form of Triceratops

facts.statement: Studies from 2011 to 2013 argued that morphological differences between Torosaurus and Triceratops prevent them from being the same species.
facts.quote: In 2011, 2012, and 2013, however, studies of external features of known specimens have claimed that morphological differences between the two genera preclude their synonymy

facts.statement: It is currently debated whether T. utahensis is a distinct genus or the mature growth stage of a Triceratops species, though this research has not yet been published.
facts.quote: Research has not yet been published on whether T. utahensis should be regarded as a new genus or, as has been suggested for T. latus, the mature growth stage of a species of Triceratops

facts.statement: Torosaurus individuals were large, measuring 7.5 to 9 meters long and weighing between 6 and 11 metric tons.
facts.quote: The individuals referred to Torosaurus are all large, comparable to the largest Triceratops specimens, measuring 7.5 to 9 m long and weighing 6 - 11 MT.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh estimated the skull of specimen YPM 1830 at 2.2 meters and YPM 1831 at 2.35 meters.
facts.quote: Hatcher estimated the skull of YPM 1830 at 2.2 m and that of YPM 1831 at 2.35 m.

facts.statement: The specimen nicknamed "Adam" has the largest known skull at 3 meters long and was first displayed in 2023.
facts.quote: The well preserved skull of the Torosaurus specimen nicknamed "Adam", first put on display in 2023, is the largest known at 3 m long.

facts.statement: In 2006, Andrew Farke noted that new skull descriptions were longer on average than Othniel Charles Marsh's original estimates.
facts.quote: In 2006, Andrew Farke had pointed out that the new skulls described by him were even longer on average than Hatcher's original two.

facts.statement: Specimen MOR 1122 has a skull length of 2.52 meters, while MOR 981 measures 2.77 meters.
facts.quote: MOR 1122 has a length of 2.52 m and MOR 981 has a length of 2.77 m.

facts.statement: The rear edge of the Torosaurus frill bears ten or more epiparietals, which are triangular osteoderms.
facts.quote: The rear edge of the frill bears ten or more epiperietals, or triangular osteoderms.

facts.statement: The parietal bone of Torosaurus is approximately 20% wider than it is long.
facts.quote: The parietal bone is about 20% wider than it is long.

facts.statement: The orbital horns of Torosaurus vary, being large and curved forward in MOR 981, or short and straight in MOR 1122 and ANSP 15191.
facts.quote: The orbital "brow" horns are sometimes large and curved to the front, as with MOR 981, or sometimes short and straight, as shown by MOR 1122 and ANSP 15191.

facts.statement: Specimen MOR 981 has ten epiparietals, and MOR 1122 has twelve.
facts.quote: MOR 981 and MOR 1122 have ten and twelve epiparietals, respectively.

facts.statement: Torosaurus has traditionally been classified in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae due to its long frill.
facts.quote: Torosaurus has, with its long frill, traditionally been classified in Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis in the 1990s showed that both Torosaurus and Triceratops belong to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: However, in the 1990s, exact cladistic analysis showed that both genera were chasmosaurines.

facts.statement: In 1998, Thomas Lehman claimed that a Pentaceratops specimen had a skull that would have been 2.9 meters long in life.
facts.quote: In 1998, however, Thomas Lehman claimed that a Pentaceratops specimen possessed a partial skull that would have been 2.9 m long in life.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke stressed that no systematic differences exist between Torosaurus and Triceratops apart from the frill.
facts.quote: Farke stressed that, apart from the frill, no systematic differences could be found between Torosaurus and Triceratops.

facts.statement: In 2008, Hunt concluded that T. utahensis possessed a midline epiparietal, unlike T. latus but similar to Triceratops.
facts.quote: In 2008, Hunt concluded that T. utahensis, contrary to T. latus, but similar to Triceratops, possessed a midline epiparietal.

facts.statement: Torosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian age in the region of Laramidia.
facts.quote: In the Maastrichtian age of Laramidia, two closely related chasmosaurines shared the same habitat.

facts.statement: The primary difference between Torosaurus and Triceratops was the shape of their frills.
facts.quote: The only discernible difference between them was the form of the frill.

facts.statement: In 2009, John Scannella hypothesized that Torosaurus and Triceratops were growth stages of a single genus based on his study of fossils in the Hell Creek Formation of Montana.
facts.quote: In 2009, John Scannella, investigating dinosaur ontogeny in the Hell Creek Formation of Montana, concluded that this situation could be best explained by the hypothesis that Triceratops and Torosaurus were growth stages of a single genus.

facts.statement: In 2010, John Scannella and Jack Horner published research analyzing thirty-eight skull specimens from the Hell Creek formation to support the idea that Torosaurus is the mature form of Triceratops.
facts.quote: In 2010, Scanella and Jack Horner, Scannella's mentor at Montana State University, published research on the growth patterns in thirty-eight skull specimens (twenty-nine of Triceratops, nine of Torosaurus) from the Hell Creek formation.

facts.statement: Jack Horner proposed that the frills of ceratopsians are made of metaplastic bone, which can change shape over time.
facts.quote: Horner stressed that the frill of ceratopsian skulls consisted of metaplastic bone.

facts.statement: Triceratops typically has five epiparietals including a midline one, whereas Torosaurus has ten or twelve without a midline epiparietal.
facts.quote: With Triceratops, there are typically five epiparietals, including a midline osteoderm. With Torosaurus, there are ten or twelve, a midline epiparietal being absent.

facts.statement: The conclusions drawn by Scannella and Horner regarding the relationship between Torosaurus and Triceratops have not been widely accepted by the scientific community.
facts.quote: Scannella and Horner's conclusions have not been widely accepted.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Torosaurus is a growth stage of Triceratops was directly challenged by papers published by Andrew Farke in 2011 and Nicholas Longrich in 2012.
facts.quote: The hypothesis was directly challenged by a 2011 paper by Andrew Farke and a 2012 paper by Nicholas Longrich.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke argued that the holes in the Nedoceratops frill were surrounded by thick swellings rather than thinning bone, contradicting the growth-stage hypothesis.
facts.quote: Farke pointed out that the irregular holes in the Nedoceratops frill, far from piercing thinning bone, were surrounded by thick swellings.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke noted that the number of epoccipitals in ceratopsians generally does not increase as the frill grows.
facts.quote: In general, the number of epoccipitals in ceratopsians does not increase when the frill grows.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke stated that the formation of holes in ceratopsian frills is not related to age, as even young individuals often possess parietal fenestrae.
facts.quote: Likewise, with Ceratopia in general, the formation of holes in the frill is not related to age, as even the youngest individuals often possess the parietal fenestrae.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke explained that the thin bone areas on Triceratops frills, previously thought to be incipient holes, are actually muscle attachment sites.
facts.quote: Farke explained the thin bone areas on the frill of Triceratops, the purported location of incipient holes, to be muscle attachment sites.

facts.statement: Researchers Farke considered the idea that Torosaurus frill holes formed after bone rejuvenation and granulation to be an unlikely sequence.
facts.quote: The bone of their frills would have to be rejuvenated and then become granulated again in order for hole formation to begin, which Farke considered to be an unlikely sequence.

facts.statement: Specimen YPM 1831 is considered a subadult Torosaurus because it has unfused sutures and smooth bone texture despite its large size.
facts.quote: Finally, Farke pointed out that specimen YPM 1831, despite its enormous size, was apparently not yet fully-grown, as shown by its unfused sutures and smooth bone texture.

facts.statement: Researchers Scanella and Horner noted that specimen USNM 2412 has holes in its frill bordered by granular and thinning bone, though they admitted it was not ideal for studying transitional forms due to pathologies.
facts.quote: They admitted that USNM 2412, in view of its pathologies, was not an ideal candidate for a transitional form, but stressed that, apart from swellings, the holes in its frill were also bordered by granular and thinning bone.

facts.statement: Scanella and Horner suggested that Nedoceratops was likely a diseased individual of Triceratops rather than a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Taking all the evidence into consideration, they thought it much more likely that Nedoceratops represented a diseased individual of Triceratops than a genus of its own.

facts.statement: Researchers proposed that the apparent doubling of epiparietals in Torosaurus could result from the erosion of osteoderm tips in older Triceratops individuals.
facts.quote: The osteoderm tips of old individuals might have eroded during life in such a way that each osteoderm gave the impression of two being present.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Torosaurus latus specimens found in older layers represent an early stage of Triceratops evolution through anagenesis.
facts.quote: Alternatively, the Torosaurus latus specimens, having been found in older layers, might, in a process of anagenesis, represent an early stage of Triceratops evolution.

facts.statement: Longrich applied the principle of falsification to the "toromorph" hypothesis, deriving three testable predictions from it.
facts.quote: Longrich argued that the "toromorph" hypothesis implied three such predictions.

facts.statement: Longrich noted that the geographical ranges of Torosaurus and Triceratops do not perfectly coincide, which supports the hypothesis that they are distinct.
facts.quote: In fact, their geographical ranges do not perfectly coincide.

facts.statement: The discrepancy in geographical ranges between Torosaurus and Triceratops might be an artifact caused by the scarcity of Torosaurus remains and imperfect sampling.
facts.quote: However, this situation could be an artefact of the relative scarcity of Torosaurus remains and imperfect sampling.

facts.statement: A 2011 study by Horner showed that investigated Triceratops specimens had subadult bone structures, but the small sample size prevented generalizing this to all fossils.
facts.quote: Admittedly, in 2011, Horner had published a histological study showing that all Triceratops specimens investigated possessed a subadult bone structure, but the sample had been too small to allow for a valid generalisation to all Triceratops fossils.

facts.statement: Analysis of skull fusion sequences indicated that most Torosaurus specimens were very old.
facts.quote: Indeed, by these criteria, most Torosaurus specimens were very old.

facts.statement: Specimen ANSP 15192 was identified as a relatively young adult Torosaurus due to the lack of fusion in its snout bones.
facts.quote: The small individual ANSP 15192 was a relatively young adult, as shown by the lack of fusion of the snout bones.

facts.statement: Specimen YPM 1831 is the youngest known Torosaurus, characterized by an unfused snout, epijugal, and occipital condyle.
facts.quote: The youngest specimen was YPM 1831, with an unfused snout, epijugal, and occipital condyle.

facts.statement: Longrich concluded that the hypothesis that Torosaurus is identical to Triceratops was refuted because mature Triceratops specimens were found to have the same level of maturation as aged Torosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Longrich concluded that the test of the second prediction refuted the hypothesis.

facts.statement: Longrich considered the claim that thin areas on Triceratops frills were precursors to parietal fenestrae as the strongest evidence for a transitional phase between the two genera.
facts.quote: Longrich considered the claim that the thin areas on Triceratops frills were precursors of parietal fenestrae, as the strongest proof of a transitional phase.

facts.statement: Longrich noted that Triceratops frill depressions are bordered by thick bone, while Torosaurus holes are surrounded by thin bone.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the depressions are bordered by much thicker bone, while the Torosaurus holes are surrounded by thin bone.

facts.statement: Longrich concluded that the hypothesis of Torosaurus being a transitional form failed based on the differences in hole location and bone thickness.
facts.quote: Longrich concluded that the hypothesis failed regarding the third prediction.

facts.statement: Longrich concluded that the hypothesis that Torosaurus is identical to Triceratops should be rejected because it was refuted by two of the three tested predictions.
facts.quote: Being refuted in two of the three predictions, the hypothesis should be rejected.

facts.statement: Torosaurus is a genus of ceratopsian ceratopsid dinosaurs represented by two species.
facts.quote: Torosaurus (lat. "lagarto perforado") es un género representado por dos especies de dinosaurios ceratopsianos ceratópsidos

facts.statement: The skull with the frill of Torosaurus measured approximately 2.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo con la gola medía alrededor de 2,8 metros de largo

facts.statement: Torosaurus was approximately 8.8 meters long, 2 meters high, and weighed between 4 and 6 tons from head to tail.
facts.quote: De la cabeza a la cola, Torosaurus debe haber rondado los 8,8 metros de largo, 2 metros de alto y haber pesado entre 4 y 6 toneladas

facts.statement: Torosaurus is distinguished by an elongated frill with large openings called fenestrae, long squamosal bones with a channel on their upper surface, and five or more pairs of epiparietal horns on the back of the frill.
facts.quote: Se distingue por un volante alargado con grandes aberturas, llamadas fenestras, huesos escamosos largos del volante con un canal en su superficie superior y la presencia de cinco o más pares de cuernos, epoccipitales, en la parte posterior del volante

facts.statement: Torosaurus had a short horn on its beak and two longer horns over its eyes, which provided protection against predators.
facts.quote: Un cuerno corto sobre su pico de loro y dos cuernos más largos sobre sus ojos que le proporciona la protección contra depredadores

facts.statement: The horns of Torosaurus were possibly used in rivalry during courtship.
facts.quote: Los cuernos también fueron utilizados posiblemente en rivalidad durante el cortejo

facts.statement: Torosaurus had the second-largest skull of any land animal, surpassed only by Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: Torosaurus fue el animal con el segundo cranéo más grande que caminó por la tierra, el que tenía el cráneo más grande fue el Pentaceratops

facts.statement: Torosaurus lacked the long nose horn seen in Triceratops prorsus and resembled the earlier Triceratops horridus by having a short nose horn.
facts.quote: Torosaurus también carecía del cuerno de nariz largo que se ve en Triceratops prorsus y en cambio se parecía al anterior y más basal Triceratops horridus por tener un cuerno de nariz corto

facts.statement: Fossils of Torosaurus have been found in western North America, from Saskatchewan to southern Texas.
facts.quote: Se han descubierto fósiles en el interior occidental de América del Norte, desde Saskatchewan hasta el sur de Texas

facts.statement: Torosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 a 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: The temporal range of Torosaurus could extend back to 69 million years ago.
facts.quote: El rango temporal podría extenderse hasta hace 69 millones de años

facts.statement: The genus Torosaurus was named by Marsh in 1891.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Marsh, 1891

facts.statement: The type species of Torosaurus is Torosaurus latus.
facts.quote: type_species: Torosaurus latus

facts.statement: Torosaurus utahensis is a subdivision of the genus, described by Lawson in 1976.
facts.quote: subdivision: Torosaurus utahensis Lawson, 1976

facts.statement: Longrich suggested objections to the hypothesis that Torosaurus represents a mature phase of Triceratops.
facts.quote: Longrich also suggested some additional objections to the "toromorph" hypothesis

facts.statement: There are no known transitional forms regarding the number of epiparietals between Torosaurus and Triceratops.
facts.quote: There are no transitional forms known regarding the number of epiparietals

facts.statement: When combined into a growth sequence, Torosaurus specimens ANSP 15192 and YPM 1831 were outliers because their squamosals were more elongated than allometry could explain.
facts.quote: Longrich pointed out that when Torosaurus and Triceratops specimens are combined to create a single growth sequence, as Scanella and Horner had done, Torosaurus specimens ANSP 15192 and YPM 1831 were outliers relative to the regression line because their squamosals were more elongated than could be explained by allometry

facts.statement: Farke's 2013 morphometric study was inconclusive regarding whether Torosaurus utahensis is a separate genus or species, as its morphospace fell between Triceratops and Torosaurus latus.
facts.quote: Farke's 2013 morphometric study was inconclusive on this point, with T. utahensis morphospace falling in between Triceratops and Torosaurus latus and not well separated from either

facts.statement: Studies in 2011, 2012, and 2013 claimed that external morphological differences between the two genera prevent their synonymy.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2011, 2012 y 2013, los estudios de características externas de especímenes conocidos han afirmado que las diferencias morfológicas entre los dos géneros impiden su sinonimia

facts.statement: Key problems preventing synonymy include a lack of good transitional forms, the apparent existence of genuine Torosaurus subadults, skull proportions independent of maturation, and hole formation in an adult stage not part of normal ceratopsian maturation.
facts.quote: Los principales problemas son la falta de buenas formas de transición, la aparente existencia de auténticos subadultos de Torosaurus, diferentes proporciones del cráneo independientes de la maduración y la formación de agujeros en una etapa adulta que no forma parte de una secuencia normal de maduración de ceratopsianos

facts.statement: Torosaurus individuals were all large, comparable to the largest Triceratops specimens.
facts.quote: Los individuos a los que se hace referencia como Torosaurus son todos grandes, comparables a los especímenes más grandes de Triceratops.

facts.statement: Hatcher estimated the skull of YPM 1830 to be 2.2 meters long and YPM 1831 to be 2.35 meters long.
facts.quote: Hatcher estimó el cráneo de YPM 1830 en 2,2 metros y el de YPM 1831 en 2,35 metros.

facts.statement: In 1933, Richard Swann Lull increased the estimated skull lengths to 2.4 meters and 2.57 meters respectively.
facts.quote: En 1933 , Richard Swann Lull aumentó esto a 2,4 metros y 2,57 metros respectivamente.

facts.statement: In 2006, Andrew Farke established some diagnostic traits for Torosaurus.
facts.quote: Farke en 2006 estableció algunos rasgos de diagnóstico de Torosaurus.

facts.statement: The frill is extremely long compared to the rest of the skull.
facts.quote: El volante es extremadamente largo en comparación con el resto del cráneo.

facts.statement: The posterior parietal edge of the frill has ten or more triangular osteoderms called epiparietals.
facts.quote: El borde posterior, parietal, del volante tiene diez o más epiparietales, osteodermos triangulares.

facts.statement: The parietal bone is thin and perforated by parietal fenestrae shaped as circular or transversely oval openings.
facts.quote: El hueso parietal es delgado. Está perforado por fenestras parietales en forma de aberturas circulares o transversalmente ovaladas.

facts.statement: The parietal bone is approximately 20% wider than it is long.
facts.quote: El hueso parietal es aproximadamente un 20% más ancho que largo.

facts.statement: Farke identified a single trait distinguishing T. latus from Triceratops horridus and T. utahensis: its squamosal had a conspicuous crest at the border with the parietal combined with a deep longitudinal canal parallel to it.
facts.quote: Farke identificó un único rasgo en el que T. latus difería tanto de Triceratops horridus como de T. utahensis, su esquamosal tenía una cresta conspicua en el borde con el parietal combinado con un profundo canal longitudinal paralelo a él.

facts.statement: The orbital 'brow' horns are sometimes large and curved forward, as in MOR 981, or sometimes short and straight, as shown in MOR 1122 and ANSP 15191.
facts.quote: Los cuernos de "ceja" orbitales son a veces grandes y curvados hacia el frente, como con MOR 981, a veces cortos y rectos como se muestra en MOR 1122 y ANSP 15191.

facts.statement: The position of these horns differs; they are often located directly above the eye socket, but in YPM 1831 they originate at the posterior edge of the orbit.
facts.quote: También la posición de estos cuernos difiere, a menudo están ubicados directamente encima del cuenca del ojo pero con YPM 1831 se originan en el borde posterior de la órbita.

facts.statement: YPM 1831 and, to a lesser extent, YPM 1830 have a straight, erect nasal horn, whereas MOR 981, ANSP 15192, and especially MOR 1122 have at most a low bump.
facts.quote: YPM 1831 y, en menor medida, YPM 1830 tienen un cuerno nasal recto y erguido, pero MOR 981, ANSP 15192 y especialmente MOR 1122, como mucho, poseen una protuberancia baja.

facts.statement: The frill of YPM 1831 is heart-shaped with a clear notch in the midline, while the posterior edge of other specimens is straight.
facts.quote: El volante de YPM 1831 también tiene forma de corazón, con una muesca clara en la línea media, mientras que el borde posterior de los otros especímenes es recto.

facts.statement: MOR 981 and MOR 1122 have ten and twelve epiparietals respectively.
facts.quote: MOR 981 y MOR 1122 tienen diez y doce epiparietales respectivamente.

facts.statement: The parent group of Torosaurus is Triceratopsini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Triceratopsini

facts.statement: Torosaurus belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Torosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Torosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 1998, Thomas Lehman claimed that a Pentaceratops specimen had a partial skull that would have been 2.9 meters long in life.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1998, Thomas Lehman afirmó que un espécimen de Pentaceratops poseía un cráneo parcial que habría tenido 2,9 metros de largo en vida.

facts.statement: In 2011, Nicholas Longrich doubted Lehman's claim, named the specimen a separate genus Titanoceratops, and concluded its skull had been reconstructed as too long.
facts.quote: Nicholas Longrich volvió a dudar de esto, quien en 2011 nombró a este ejemplar como un género separado Titanoceratops y concluyó que su cráneo había sido reconstruido como demasiado largo.

facts.statement: Farke emphasized that, apart from the frill, no systematic differences could be found between Torosaurus and Triceratops.
facts.quote: Farke enfatizó que, aparte del volante, no se pudieron encontrar diferencias sistemáticas entre Torosaurus y Triceratops.

facts.statement: In 2008, Hunt concluded that T. utahensis, contrary to T. latus but similar to Triceratops, possessed a midline epiparietal.
facts.quote: Hunt en 2008 concluyó que T. utahensis , contrario a T. latus pero similar a Triceratops, poseía un epiparietal de línea media.
